about.title: Vista Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Vista sits where SR-78 threads through northern San Diego County, and that highway, along with E Vista Way, S Melrose Drive, and Vista Village Drive, accounts for the largest share of the city's reported collisions. In 2025, public records show 212 injury collisions in Vista, with 311 people hurt and 4 lives lost. Reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters heading home mix with weekend traffic. If you were one of those 311 people, the days after a crash can feel like paperwork stacked on top of pain. Adjusters call quickly. Repair estimates arrive. Medical bills follow. We handle Vista car accident claims directly, so you can talk with us about what happened on Melrose or the 78, and we explain how California's pure comparative fault rule and two-year filing deadline apply to your situation. Our team works on contingency—you pay no fee unless we recover for you.

whyChoose.title: What We Can Do for Your Vista Car Accident Claim

items.title: Keep the two-year clock from running out
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit, but a claim involving a public agency can require notice in as little as six months. We track those dates so a missed deadline never decides your case.

items.title: Push back when fault gets shared
items.desc: Under pure comparative fault, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame, with your award reduced by your percentage. Insurers often try to inflate that percentage, and we work to keep the split honest.

items.title: Protect your evidence and your words
items.desc: Photos from the scene, dashcam footage, and witness names fade fast, and a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used against you. We preserve what helps and handle the adjuster so you don't have to.

items.question: My crash happened on SR-78 in Vista. Does it matter that it's a state highway?
items.answer: It can. SR-78 is maintained by Caltrans, so if a road condition or a government vehicle played a role, part of your claim may involve a public entity, and California requires a government claim within six months rather than the usual two years. Most SR-78 collisions are simply between private drivers, but we can sort out which rules apply to yours quickly.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise not to before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rule. Let your own insurer know about the crash as your policy requires, and let us handle the rest.

items.question: What does it cost to work with you?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. We handle car accident cases on contingency, which means we are paid a percentage of any recovery and you owe no attorney fee if there is none.
